newsitem.title: JAPAN: Weaker yen helps slow plunge in Japan surplus.
newsitem.headline: Weaker yen helps slow plunge in Japan surplus.

text.p: A weaker yen has built a barricade against a flood of cheap imports into Japan, causing the plunge in the nation's massive trade surplus to level off, a Bank of Japan (BOJ) report said on Friday.

"The decline in the trade surplus in real terms seems to have taken a breather and the current account surplus in the July-September period is most likely to have expanded slightly," the BOJ's quarterly economic outlook said.
Imports in real terms continue to be high, but the pace of increase has become moderate as the impact of the yen's depreciation against the dollar began to penetrate, it said.
A weaker yen makes imports more expensive while at the same time raising the competitiveness of Japanese exports.

Meanwhile, exports in real terms remain virtually unchanged from the middle of last year, but there are signs that it may revert to a moderate growth trend helped by the impact of the weaker yen and a stop in the falling demand for integrated circuits, the report said.
A senior BOJ official told reporters that looking at the movements in the past two to three months, exports are slowly starting to grow, as in the case of automobiles.
Pre-Christmas holiday shopping in the United States seemed to have got off to a good start, which should also help Japanese exports in the coming months, he added.
"The surplus has generally levelled off," he said.
But the central bank would need to look at more data before being certain that the shrinking trend has ended, as seasonal factors may have played a part in the recent trend, the official added.

"The halt in the falling trend would soon appear and the surplus will start rising again, perhaps, roughly around January to March period next year," said Shunsuke Motani, an economist at Sphynx Investment Research Inc.

The latest Ministry of Finance data shows Japan's customs-cleared trade surplus in September fell 30.3 percent from a year earlier to 779.52 billion yen ($6.89 billion), for the 22nd consecutive month of year-on-year declines.
In August, the trade surplus fell 34.5 percent from a year earlier and in July 38.4 percent.
The current account, the broadest measure of trade in goods and services, was 460.60 billion yen ($4.07 billion) in August, down 28.9 percent from a year before. ($1=113 yen)
